open_questions: Mass unknown: needs RV to rule out brown dwarf/small-star companion below transit detection threshold.
QLP depth 18419 ppm vs TESS-SPOC 9419 ppm offset needs confirmation in future sectors/pipeline.
dossier.public_summary: Four shallow 12.7-day dips have a flat bottom and planet-sized depth around a small 0.35 solar-radius M dwarf, with no odd-even difference or neighbour blend to explain them. The apparently deeper signal in one sector is a catalog pipeline offset, steady within the same product. The light-curve match is a planet, but mass has not yet been measured.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed transit favours planet over V-shaped grazing binary/small-star eclipse.
Planet-sized (TIC radius) and still 4.98/5.11 Rearth with Gaia FLAME/GSP-Phot radius, below 10 Rearth planet threshold.
No odd/even depth difference; depth_odd_ppm 12990 vs depth_even_ppm 12070 ratio 1.1 rules out EB at twice period.
Below 5 threshold and not well above best_brightening_snr 3.534; no significant secondary at phase 0.3499.
No neighbour within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can cause dip with eclipse <=25%; closest that could is 51.4 arcsec needing 0.0166 eclipse.

Apparently variable depth 7532, 10861, 18419 ppm, but sector_depths_by_source verdict differs_by_source: TESS-SPOC p_constant 0.331 steady (7532/10861 consistent within errors) vs QLP 18419 ppm in one sector — calibration offset, not astrophysical change.
Four transits depths inconsistent at low SNR 11.3, but outliers [] none flagged and refit SNR 11.3 still above 7; inconsistency consistent with per-sector depth offset, not few bad events.
